documentation.rationale: The identity and terms half is present: published VIN that decodes correctly, clean DC title claimed, Carfax snapshot with owner count and damage disclosure, no reserve, $0 dealer fees. The maintenance half is missing: no receipts, the 21 Carfax records are not shown, and the top replacement and tires are seller-only claims. Nothing covers the model's cooling or oil-leak weak points.

condition.rationale: Photos show clean paint, a clean oyster interior, healthy-looking tires and a tidy engine bay. A rear underside photo shows grime but no visible heavy rust. Against that: Carfax roof damage, a repainted bumper and trunk, disclosed paint imperfections and wheel curb marks. No cooling, oil-leak or PPI evidence is offered.

mission_fit.rationale: This matches the profile's primary bridge: manual, naturally aspirated BMW six, M Sport, likely to land inside the $10k–$19k ideal band, with easy resale. Inspection access before close is unconfirmed, and the cooling history on a car this age is open.

positives: Factory six-speed manual with the naturally aspirated 3.0L six and M Sport Package, the profile's target spec, in final-year 2013 form.
Published VIN decodes cleanly. Carfax 1-owner with 21 service records listed. Clean DC title. No reserve and $0 dealer fees.
Photos show a clean, stock-appearing engine bay, an unworn oyster interior and healthy-looking tires (Hankook, mounted 2026 per seller).
Seller is engaged, has posted driving and top-operation videos, and disclosed the damage, repaints and paint imperfections up front.
Oil changed October 2026, per the listing.
concerns: Observed: Carfax reports 'very minor' roof damage (January 2026), and the front bumper cover and trunk have been repainted. No repair invoices, cause or repaint reason are given.
Observed: Convertible top replaced 'in preparation for the sale' per the seller, with no invoice. Ask whether this relates to the roof damage, and check top seals and drains for water ingress.
Observed: Curb marks on the Style 207M wheels and disclosed paint finish imperfections (cosmetic).
Unverified: Electric water pump, thermostat and expansion tank history (ask for Carfax lines/receipts; inspect the pump and look for coolant traces).
Unverified: Oil-filter-housing, valve-cover and oil-pan leak status (inspect from below with the undertray off).
Unverified: Completion of the two Takata airbag inflator recalls (16V071, 20V017) and the PCV heater recall (22V119) (ask for proof from a BMW dealer VIN lookup).
unknowns: Full Carfax report: contents of the 21 service records, registration states, and how the roof damage arose.
Water pump and thermostat replacement date and mileage.
Oil-leak condition of the oil-filter-housing gasket, valve-cover gasket and oil pan.
Front underside, floor pans and jack points on this Northeast car (not examined here).
Whether the emissions label shows CA certification.
Whether a third-party PPI is permitted before the auction closes.
seller_questions: Can you post or send the full Carfax so the 21 service records and the January 2026 roof damage entry can be read line by line?
Has the electric water pump or thermostat ever been replaced? If so, at what date and mileage, with an invoice?
Are there any oil seeps at the oil-filter-housing gasket, valve-cover gasket or oil pan? Can you post photos from below with the undertray removed?
What caused the roof damage recorded in January 2026, and was the replacement top installed because of it? Who installed it, and is there an invoice?
Why were the front bumper cover and trunk repainted? Was any panel, sensor or bracket replaced?
What are the DOT date codes on all four Hankook tires?
Can you provide a BMW dealer printout showing the airbag recalls 16V071 and 20V017 and the PCV recall 22V119 as completed?
Can you post a full-system scan (fault codes) and a cold-start video from fully cold, with the hood open?
Will you allow a third-party pre-purchase inspection at a nearby shop before the auction closes on October 20?
Can you photograph the under-hood emissions label to confirm whether the car is California/SULEV certified?
Does the top seal without leaks? Have the top drains been cleared, and is there any dampness under the rear seat or in the trunk?
ppi_focus: Electric water pump and thermostat: age and part dates, live-data coolant temperature and pump speed, any coolant crust at the pump, expansion tank or hoses.
Oil-filter-housing gasket, valve-cover gasket and oil pan, including any oil reaching the drive belt or alternator area.
Roof and top: frame alignment, seals, drains, top operation, and water ingress in the rear footwells and trunk, given the roof damage entry and the replaced top.
Paint meter on all panels to confirm that only the bumper and trunk were refinished; check trunk gaps and seams for collision repair.
Full fault-code scan, including the DME, the airbag module and the convertible top module.
Clutch engagement point, slip test, and dual-mass flywheel noise at idle.
Underside of a Northeast car: jack points, floor pans, brake and fuel lines, subframe mounts, plus the front control-arm and thrust-arm bushings.
Recall verification by VIN at a BMW dealer, with particular attention to the Takata airbag recalls.
Tire date codes and wheels: confirm the curb marks are cosmetic and none of the rims is bent.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: the full Carfax or receipts show water pump and thermostat replacement and oil-leak gasket work, plus completed recalls.
Up: an independent PPI before close finds a dry engine, a sealed top, paint confined to the disclosed panels and a clean scan.
Down: the PPI or the seller cannot be arranged, or the roof damage turns out to involve structural or top-frame repair.
Down: active coolant loss, oil leaks, or a slipping clutch found at inspection.
evidence.mission_note: This is the profile's primary enthusiast-bridge spec: manual, naturally aspirated six, M Sport, likely to hammer inside the ideal band, and easy to resell in 6–24 months. Accelerated-bridge mode still calls for a PPI before bidding rather than buying on photos.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes the car's identity and terms well: the published VIN decodes as a 2013 128i convertible, the title is a clean DC title, the Carfax snapshot shows 1 owner, 21 service records and a 52,106-mile reading, and the auction is no reserve with $0 dealer fees. Photos confirm a six-speed manual, M Sport equipment, a clean oyster interior and a tidy, stock-appearing engine bay. Observed issues are disclosed by the listing itself: a January 2026 Carfax 'very minor' roof damage entry, a repainted front bumper and trunk, a convertible top replaced before sale per the seller, curb-marked wheels and paint imperfections. None of these comes with repair documentation. The model's critical weak points remain open: nothing shows the electric water pump, thermostat or oil-leak history, and the underside photo covers only the rear of the car. Tires (2026) and an October 2026 oil change are stated but unreceipted. Recall completion for two airbag campaigns and the PCV recall is unknown.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller today requesting the full Carfax, cooling and gasket service records, tire date codes and recall printout, and ask permission to book an independent PPI near Marlboro, NY before the October 20 close.
